passages.note: Senate roll call 520 shows Donato voting Yea on the Conference Committee Report for HB 1447, a multi-subject 'education matters' bill; the tally page does not print the library provision.

passages.provision_quote: The governing body of a school corporation or charter school shall establish a: (1) procedure for each school to prepare a catalogue of materials available in the school library; (2) procedure for each school to allow a: (A) parent or guardian of a student enrolled in the school; or (B) community member: (i) within the school district; or (ii) within the school district in which the charter school is located; to submit a request to remove material from the school library that is obscene (as described in IC 35-49-2-1) or harmful to minors (as described in IC 35-49-2-2); and (3) response and appeal procedure for each school to respond to a removal request submitted by a parent, guardian, or community member described in subdivision (2).
passages.note: SECTION 2 of the enrolled act creates a school-library removal-request procedure limited to material that is obscene or harmful to minors, reviewed by the governing body, inside a bill that also covers Muncie school exemptions, student surveys, and classroom neutrality.
The bill-details page names Donato as Senate sponsor of HB 1447; its own digest text describes the third-party-survey provision, not the library provision.

rows.reasoning: Donato voted Yea on the Conference Committee Report for HB 1447 (2023), a multi-subject 'education matters' bill, and is named as Senate sponsor; SECTION 2 of the enrolled act creates a school-library removal-request procedure for material that is obscene or harmful to minors, reviewed by the governing body, among several unrelated provisions (Muncie school exemptions, third-party student surveys, classroom neutrality). Under the multi-subject vote rule her vote and sponsorship show direction at most, not a specific rung, absent her own statement tying support to the library clause specifically.
